title: Gandhi Irwin Pact
definition: A political agreement signed on March 5, 1931, between Mahatma Gandhi and Lord Irwin, representing the British Government, which marked the end of the Civil Disobedience Movement and paved the way for Congress participation in the Second Round Table Conference.
importanceInUpsc: It is a pivotal turning point in the Indian National Movement, testing the candidate's understanding of the 'Truce-Struggle-Truce' strategy and the complex negotiations between colonial authority and nationalist leadership.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Gandhi Irwin Pact.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Role of Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jayakar
